paper.title: Learning to Attack: A Bandit Approach to Adversarial Context Poisoning

settings.name_in_paper: Attacker's continuous-armed bandit over attack parameters lambda in [0,1]^3 (GP-UCB with contextual state)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Guarantee for an attacker (context-poisoning adversary) rather than for the bandit learner.
unmapped: Attacker poisons contexts of a victim neural contextual bandit; attacker's reward depends on the evolving victim policy
Contextual state built from an IRL surrogate of the victim (approximate states); IRL misspecification error eps_mis
Attack budget B limits number of attack rounds n <= B
settings.definition_quote: we formalize the attack as a bilevel problem over a continuous arm space $\boldsymbol{\Lambda} = [0,1]^3$ ... The attacker's reward function $r(\mathbf{s},\boldsymbol{\lambda})$ lies in the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_k$ with bounded norm $\|r\|_{\mathcal{H}_k} \leq B_{\textsc{rkhs}}$, and observations are corrupted by $\sigma_n$-sub-Gaussian noise.

settings.name_in_paper: Victim K-armed neural contextual bandit (R-NeuralUCB) under context poisoning attack
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Result quantifies the damage achieved by an attacker (lower bound on the victim's regret under a specific attack), a guarantee for the attacker rather than the learner.
unmapped: Contexts perturbed by an attacker with l_inf bound epsilon and attack budget B
Reward h is L_h-Lipschitz in context with values in [0,1]
Victim is the specific algorithm R-NeuralUCB
settings.definition_quote: In a $K$-armed contextual bandit setting with horizon $T$ ... receives a reward $r_{t,a_t} = h(\mathbf{x}_{t,a_t}) + \xi_t$ ... The attacker perturbs the context of each arm ... $\|\boldsymbol{\delta}_{t,i}\|_\infty \leq \epsilon$, subject to a total attack budget $B$

algorithms.name: AdvBandit (GP-UCB attack parameter selection with MaxEnt IRL surrogate, query selection and PGD)

symbols.n_att: number of attack rounds (n <= attack budget)
symbols.gamma_n: maximum information gain after n rounds, O((log n)^{d_gp+1}) for SE kernel
symbols.d_Theta: number of IRL parameters, O(d d_h K)

conditions: Approximate realizability (Assumption 5.3) with misspecification error eps_mis
attacker reward r(s, lambda) in RKHS of SE kernel with bounded norm
victim is R-NeuralUCB-type with O(1/sqrt t) confidence widths

source.label: thm:attacker_regret_full
source.quote: Let $\boldsymbol{\lambda}^*(\mathbf{s}) = \arg\max_{\boldsymbol{\lambda}} r(\mathbf{s},\boldsymbol{\lambda})$. Under Assumption~\ref{assm:approx_real}, with probability at least $1-\rho$, the attacker's cumulative regret over $n$ attack rounds satisfies: R_attack(n) \le O(\sqrt{n \gamma_n \log(n/\rho)}) + O(\sqrt{n} \sqrt{d_\Theta/W}) + O(\sqrt{n \Delta_{irl}}) + n \epsilon_{mis}. ... Under exact realizability ($\epsilon_{mis} = 0$), this simplifies to $R_{attack}(n) \leq O(\sqrt{n \gamma_n \log(n/\rho)} + \sqrt{n})$.

results.notes: Attacker-side guarantee (out of scope). Regret is against lambda*(s) per state. Proof is sketchy/heuristic. Simplified exact-realizability form O(sqrt(n gamma_n log(n/rho)) + sqrt(n)) needs W = Omega(d_Theta) and constant Delta_IRL; not recorded separately.

bound.expression_latex: R_v(T) \geq B \cdot \bar{\alpha} - O(\sqrt{B} \sqrt{d_\Theta/W}) - O(\sqrt{B \Delta_{irl}}) - O(\sqrt{T \log T})

symbols.alpha_bar: average positive attackability margin (1/B) sum_{attacked t} [Delta(x_t, a_t^dagger) - 2 L_h epsilon]^+
symbols.d_Theta: number of IRL parameters, O(d d_h K)

conditions: victim algorithm is R-NeuralUCB with O(sqrt T) unattacked regret
attacker runs AdvBandit with budget B, perturbation bound epsilon
true reward h: R^d -> [0,1] is L_h-Lipschitz in context

source.label: thm:victim_regret
source.quote: With attack budget $B$, perturbation bound $\epsilon$, and IRL retraining interval $\Delta_{\textsc{irl}}$ with window size $W$, the victim's cumulative regret satisfies with probability at least $1-\rho$: R_v(T) \geq B \cdot \bar{\alpha} - O(\sqrt{B} \cdot \sqrt{d_\Theta/W}) - O(\sqrt{B \cdot \Delta_{irl}}) - O(\sqrt{T \log T}).

results.notes: Lower bound on the victim's regret induced by the specific AdvBandit attack against R-NeuralUCB, not a minimax lower bound for learners. Subtracted terms carry hidden constants (O(.)), recorded via Omega notation. Corollary F.3 (profitability condition B > O(sqrt(T log T))/(alpha_bar - O(sqrt(d_Theta/W)))) follows from it.
